hints: Notice that both compounds are aldehydes, so focus on what structural difference remains between them.
Ethanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ and contains a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group, while propanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ and does not.
Recall which test gives a yellow precipitate only with the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group and think about what you would see for each aldehyde.
walkthrough:
**Spot what is the same**

Both ethanal and propanal are aldehydes. They both contain the $\text{-CHO}$ group, so any test for aldehydes in general will be positive for both.

Structures:
$$\text{ethanal} = \text{CH}_3\text{CHO}, \quad \text{propanal} = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$$

**Rule out the general tests**

2,4-DNPH tests for any carbonyl, acidified dichromate oxidises any aldehyde, and Tollens oxidises any aldehyde. All three will do the same thing to ethanal and propanal, so they cannot distinguish them.

**Use the special methyl group test**

The triiodomethane (iodoform) test with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH(aq)}$ is positive only for molecules containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$.

Reaction for ethanal:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{HCOONa} + 3\text{NaI} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Compare the observations**

Ethanal has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ unit, so it forms a pale yellow precipitate of triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$. Propanal has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$, so it stays as a colourless solution with no precipitate. This clear difference distinguishes them.

options.A: 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine gives an orange precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone. Both ethanal and propanal will give this result, so no distinction is seen.
options.B: I2 in NaOH(aq) is the iodoform test. Ethanal contains CH3CO and gives a pale yellow precipitate of CHI3, while propanal does not contain this group and gives no precipitate. This is a clear positive versus negative result.
options.C: Acidified K2Cr2O7 is an oxidising agent that oxidises both aldehydes to carboxylic acids. Both will turn the solution from orange to green, so they cannot be distinguished.
options.D: Tollens reagent is reduced by all aldehydes to give a silver mirror. Both ethanal and propanal are aldehydes, so both give the silver mirror and no distinction is possible.
